subject: Cumulus renewal: pricing options + optional capacity expansion
messages:
From: Alicia Barnes <alicia@cumulus.ai>
To: mina_haddad@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 20 Mar 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal: pricing + capacity ask

Hi Mina,

Hope you had a good week. We’re starting our renewal planning for the account and wanted to get a sense of pricing options: our usage is up ~35% year-over-year and the team expects another ~30% increase if we add seats for the new recommendation engine.

High-level asks:
- 12-month renewal with an option to increase committed capacity by ~30% midway through term (we need a clear uplift path)
- Any possibility of a price-hold for 12 months while we stabilize usage
- One-off credits for the months we significantly exceeded commit this quarter (Q1 overage)

Can you send a couple of concrete proposal options (discounts, credits, commit changes) we can review before procurement/finance gets involved? Goal is to finalize in the next two weeks.

Thanks,
Alicia
Alicia Barnes
Head of ML Platforms, Cumulus Analytics
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Barnes <alicia@cumulus.ai>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, rohan_mehta@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 20 Mar 2027 17:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal: pricing + capacity ask

Hi Alicia — thanks for the heads up and congrats on the surge in usage. We can absolutely put together a focused set of options. Two quick asks from our side to make the proposals concrete:
- Can you confirm current committed daily throughput / tokens and the approximate monthly $ run rate under the current contract?
- Are you aiming for a pure 12-month commercially-bound renewal, or would you consider a 24-month commitment if we provide a stronger price hold?

I’ve looped in Rishi (AE) and Rohan (Sales Ops) to help with discounts, credits, and the capacity uplift math. I’ll aim to get two clearly scoped options back to you by EOD Tuesday so you can run internal review. If it helps, we can also do a 30-minute walkthrough on Wednesday.

Best,

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>

Subject: FW: Cumulus renewal: pricing options + optional capacity expansion

Team — forwarding Alicia’s note. Quick summary / recommended approach before I draft external proposals:

Customer asks:
- 12-month renewal; wants optional +30% capacity uplift mid-term
- Price-hold if possible for 12 months
- One-time credits for Q1 overage months

Recommended packages (two clean options for customer-facing PDF):

Option 1 — Short-term protect (12m)
- 12-month term
- 20% discount off list for committed usage aligned to their current run rate
- 10% credit applied to invoice(s) for Q1 overages (applied as one-time credit)
- Optional mid-term capacity uplift: allow one-off increase at prorated rates up to +30% with 90-day notice

Option 2 — Price-hold ramp (24m)
- 24-month term with price hold for months 1–12
- Smaller up-front discount (12%) but guaranteed list price hold months 1–12
- Quarterly capacity ramp schedule baked into SOW (10% increases per quarter until +30%)
- No overage credit, but larger commit floor reduces unit price overall

Questions for Sales Ops / Finance (Rohan):
- Margin impact and acceptability of a $ credit vs larger discount?
- Can we include a one-time onboarding credit if they sign by EOM? (helps close quickly)

Please review and push back — once we align I’ll create a one-page PDF for Alicia and a more detailed workbook for procurement/legal.

Thanks,
Mina

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: mina_haddad@redwood.com
Cc: rohan_mehta@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 21 Mar 2027 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FW: Cumulus renewal: pricing options + optional capacity expansion

Agree with the two-option approach. A couple of tactical tweaks that helped close similar deals last quarter: 
- Move Option 1 discount from 20% to 18% and sweeten with a one-time onboarding credit: $15,000 applied to first invoice if deal executes by 2027-03-31.
- For Option 2, ensure the price-hold has an explicit rollback clause tied to usage >2.0x baseline (protects us if they hyper-scale).

I’ll pick up procurement/legal introductions once we have the chosen option. Also suggest we include a short SLA addendum for latency-sensitive endpoints they mentioned.

Deal: DEAL-2027-3047

From: Rohan Mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.com>

Date: Sun, 21 Mar 2027 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FW: Cumulus renewal: pricing options + optional capacity expansion

Running margins and attached a simple calc (attachment stub: cumulus_pricing_calc.xlsx). Key points from ops review:
- Baseline commit today: 85k tokens/day equivalent; projected +30% -> ~110k tokens/day
- Option 1 (18% discount + $15k credit) preserves target margin at ~28% after credits; acceptable to finance
- Option 2 (24m price-hold) reduces near-term margin to ~24% but improves LTV and reduces churn risk if they lock for 24m

Recommendation: Lead with Option 1 externally (faster sign), highlight Option 2 as escalation for Procurement/Finance if they push for price-hold.

Attachments: cumulus_pricing_calc.xlsx (SKU-level math, prorated uplift table)
Rohan

Subject: Cumulus Renewal — two proposed options and next steps

Hi Alicia (and Procurement team),

Thanks for the context — attached are two concise options for your review (attached PDF + the SKU calc). Summary below so you can share with Finance/Procurement quickly.

Option A — Short-term protect (recommended, faster cadence)
- Term: 12 months
- Committed baseline: current run rate (85k tokens/day), with optional +30% uplift granted once during term with 90-day notice
- Commercials: 18% discount off list on committed usage; one-time onboarding credit $15,000 applied to first invoice if signed by 2027-03-31
- Q1 overage: 10% credit applied to Q1 invoices to account for exceptional overages

Option B — Price-hold ramp (procurement-friendly)
- Term: 24 months; price hold for months 1–12
- Commercials: 12% discount off list; ramp schedule to reach +30% capacity over first 3 quarters
- No Q1 credit; larger commit floor reduces unit price over life

Attached: Cumulus_Renewal_Proposal.pdf (one-page choices) and cumulus_pricing_calc.xlsx (breakdown). I’ve also included a DocuSign link to a redline-friendly SOW if you prefer to move forward quickly: https://docusign.com/link/ABC-123-CUMULUS

Next steps:
1) Please confirm which option you prefer and whether procurement would like the 24m price-hold variant for negotiation.
2) If Option A, confirm by EOD 2027-03-31 for the $15k onboarding credit to apply.
3) If procurement requests, we’ll provide a redline SOW and loop legal (Rishi will own that thread).

Feel free to schedule a 30-minute walkthrough: https://calendly.com/mina-redwood/30m

Best,
